James was going through a rough financial patch. He struggled to make ends meet and had no savings left. One morning, he received an unexpected email from a government welfare agency he had applied to months ago. "Congratulations! You have been selected for financial assistance. You will be receiving the full aid amount to help with your expenses."

As James went to the agency to collect, he found Mark, a neighbor. He learned that Mark also applied but wasn't selected. Only James received the funds.

Now James faced a choice. Should he keep all the money for himself? James was tempted because he really needed the money, and Mark was just an acquaintance. Or should he give some of it to Mark, given that he was struggling? What should he do?

vignettes.text: Chiara and Stefano are offered a one-time payment for a community project they developed together, but the sponsor will release the money only if they agree on its division. Chiara is wary of the risk that Stefano might decline, but she also sees the project as a great win-win situation for both. Thus, she proposes a good share to Stefano, which still leaves a very good profit for her. Stefano accepts and Chiara is very happy.

Miriam and Roberto discover a box of collectible books being sold cheaply at a clearance sale. Miriam has the cash to buy them, while Roberto knows collectors who would pay much more for the books and has offered to handle the resale. Miriam decides to finance half of the available purchase. She views the decision as a matter of fairness and moral principle: since Roberto is also contributing to the opportunity, she thinks that giving him an equal stake is the morally right thing to do. After the books are sold, Roberto sends part of the proceeds back to Miriam.

Two firms complete preparatory work for an order that is later cancelled. The platform offers a fixed compensation payment, but it will release the money only if both firms agree on how it is divided. Firm A is asked to propose the split. Its manager views the decision as a matter of fairness and moral principle, because both firms incurred costs preparing for the order. She thinks that the morally right thing to do is an equal split, and proposes it. Firm B accepts and the payment is shared.

Anna and Marco helped organize a neighborhood festival. The association later sends Anna a bundle of meal vouchers as a thank-you and tells her that she may keep them all or pass some on to Marco. Anna gives Marco half. They both put a lot of time into the event, and she feels it is fair to share the reward between them. She views this as a matter of moral principle and thinks that an equal split is the morally right thing to do in this situation.

A producer and a distributor are considering a one-time order that will create a substantial margin if the deal goes through. The producer proposes how that margin will be divided, and the distributor can reject, in which case the order is lost and neither firm earns anything. The producer sees agreement as a very profitable opportunity for both sides and proposes a good share to the distributor. The producer’s manager is wary of the risk of rejection, but optimistic. She is right: the terms are accepted, making the deal very valuable for her firm.

The platform pays the entire completion bonus to Firm A and leaves any transfer to B at A's discretion. The manager views the match as a value-creating collaboration made possible by the firms' complementary contributions and shares the completion bonus with Firm B.

Martina sees agreement as a valuable win-win opportunity for her and Enrico. At the same time, he really needs this money and why would she reject, given that a small payment is better than no payment at all?  He therefore seizes the opportunity to maximize his own profit and offers Giulia only a small share. Giulia accepts and Luca keeps most for himself.
